summary: Operation comparison for bounded constructible coefficients: strict integral reduction, derived mapping limits for trace and Gysin morphisms, finite coefficient extension, complex orientation and supported classes, analytic smooth trace compatibility, and scheme/diamond trace mates. Existing EDC.6 categories and comparisons are imported by their original ids. Generic adic realization remains with CohomologicalPointCounting/EllAdicRealization, integrated through SF.2. Strong diamond exceptional-pullback transport is explicitly conditional on essential-image preservation; stacks and perfect-space extensions keep their inherited Part II owners.

nodes.title: Strict reduction of integral exceptional pullback and duality
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with ℓ invertible, O the integers of a finite extension of Q_ℓ, λ a uniformizer, O_n=O/λ^n (n≥1), and f:X→Y a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type k-schemes. In the imported normalized constructible adic/pro-étale category write ρ_nK=K⊗^L_O O_n and K_X=a_X^!O. The canonical comparisons ρ_n f^!K≃f_n^!ρ_nK, ρ_n Rf_*M≃Rf_{n,*}ρ_nM, and ρ_n Rf_!M≃Rf_{n,!}ρ_nM hold. Completed pullback and tensor commute with reduction; internal Hom satisfies ρ_n RHom_O(M,N)≃RHom_{O_n}(ρ_nM,ρ_nN). Consequently ρ_nK_X≃a_X^!O_n, ρ_nD_XM≃D_{X,n}ρ_nM, and the integral biduality map is an isomorphism. These comparisons respect identity, composition and repeated reduction. Outputs are bounded constructible, with one finite stratification and ordinary/Tor bounds independent of n.
hypotheses: K,M,N are bounded constructible derived-complete O-complexes with perfect stalks on finite strata; over the regular DVR O this includes bounded finitely generated stalk complexes and integral torsion.

Finite-type schemes over a field are noetherian, excellent and finite dimensional. The finite cohomological dimension used for direct images is that of the relative étale pushforward, supplied by the finite-level finiteness theorem, not an assertion about arithmetic global cohomology.
Internal Hom is sheaf internal Hom. A constructible object supported on a stratum need not be globally tensor-dualizable. Restrict bounded coefficient operations through actual finite-Tor witnesses.
proofSteps: Import the homotopy-coherent normalized-system/pro-étale equivalence and reduction functors from the existing EDC.6 category nodes through SF.2. EllAdicRealization Layers 0–6 supply Z_ℓ/Q_ℓ realization and geometric finiteness; the exact finite O/E extension of that owner is separately requested.

Apply Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.1 to obtain finite relative cohomological dimension and 6.5.11 for strict Rf_* reduction. Use a compactification, finite-level proper support and 6.7.6–6.7.10 for Rf_!; do not identify Rf_! with the right derived functor of H^0f_! on the pro-étale site.

For f^!, use 6.7.18: locally factor f as a closed immersion followed by a smooth map. Smooth purity gives reduction on the smooth factor; the closed factor uses the localization triangle and direct-image scalar comparison for its open complement. Then 6.7.19 constructs the compatible limit and its adjunction.
Apply 6.7.13 by stratified dévissage for internal Hom and use f=a_X for K_X. Reduce biduality to the finite-level EDC.1:biduality map and use conservativity on derived-complete objects.

The noetherian stratification criterion 6.6.11 gives common strata; local perfect O-complexes give uniform Tor bounds for reductions. Coherence comes from the canonical exchange maps in the enhanced imported formalism.
acceptance: At a geometric point, the object O/λ in degree zero is admitted; its derived O_n-reduction has nonzero degrees −1 and 0, so reduction is not ordinary tensor on cohomology.
For smooth f of relative dimension d, the comparison reduces f^!O=O(d)[2d] to O_n(d)[2d], preserving the trace-normalized purity map.
For a smooth closed divisor and its open complement, reduction commutes with the supported localization triangle.

sources.match: Finite cohomological dimension upgrades a pro-system comparison to strict reduction. Stratification and local closed/smooth factorization give the exceptional-pullback and internal-Hom comparisons needed for integral duality.

The generic limit, Z_ℓ/Q_ℓ normalized coefficient realization and geometric finite-type bounds are imported targets of this owner. Common-stratum O/E constructible realization and its coherent categorical interface require the recorded extension, not a claim that PR196 already states them.

nodes.title: Coherent mapping limits for integral traces and cycle classes
nodes.statement: Let X be separated finite type over a separably closed field k, ℓ invertible in k, and M,N in the bounded constructible derived-complete O-category above. With M_n=ρ_nM, N_n=ρ_nN, the canonical equivalence of derived O-module mapping complexes is RHom_X(M,N)≃Rlim_n RHom_{X,O_n}(M_n,N_n). Thus 0→lim¹_n Hom(M_n,N_n[−1])→Hom_X(M,N)→lim_n Hom(M_n,N_n)→0. Finite-level shifted Hom groups are finite, so the lim¹ term vanishes in this geometric setting. Compatible finite-level traces, evaluation/biduality maps, cup products, smooth-pair Gysin morphisms and supported cycle classes give unique integral maps with these reductions; their finite-level naturality, composition and projection identities hold integrally. The maps agree under the classical/pro-étale realization equivalence and rationalize to the E-valued maps. Integral derived cohomology retains the Tor and Ext terms of coefficient reduction and duality.
hypotheses: O is a finite-extension integer ring as above; coefficients are finite at each level and objects have common finite strata, coherent reductions and uniform ordinary/Tor bounds.

RHom_X denotes RΓ(X,RHom_O(M,N)), not only sheaf internal Hom. Finiteness and the degreewise Hom-limit identity use separably closed k. For arithmetic k retain the derived mapping equivalence when its imported hypotheses hold and the displayed lim¹ obstruction; no unconditional equality detection is asserted.

Relative natural transformations are first supplied with enhanced compatibility/homotopies. The geometric Hom-limit consequence applies to each specified pair of objects; it is not a replacement for coherent functor-level data.
proofSteps: Use strict internal-Hom reduction and the homotopy-coherent normalized realization requested through SF.2. EllAdicRealization Layers 0–2 and 6 supply the generic derived-limit and geometric-finiteness inputs; retain the requested finite O/E coefficient extension.

Apply the Milnor sequence to the derived mapping complex. Finite-level constructibility and geometric cohomological finiteness imply every shifted Hom group is finite; descending images in each finite group stabilize, proving Mittag–Leffler rather than assuming surjective transition maps.

Lift the specified compatible finite-level morphisms through this mapping equivalence. Compare both sides of an identity by their coherent reductions and use the vanishing lim¹ term. For adjunction and purity use their canonical enhanced maps, not arbitrary choices of lifts.

Import the integral derived Poincaré-duality statement and its Ext¹ sequence from EDC.2:pairings/adic-and-rational-poincare-duality. For a perfect O-complex C, retain 0→H^q(C)⊗O_n→H^q(C⊗^LO_n)→H^{q+1}(C)[λ^n]→0. Flat rationalization removes the torsion only after these integral statements have been established.
acceptance: On a point take C=O/λ in degree zero. RHom_O(C,O) has H¹=O/λ and H⁰=0; C⊗^LO_n has H⁻¹ and H⁰ both O/λ. A rational-only pairing would erase this test.
For P¹, the integral trace of c₁(O(1)) is 1, and every reduction gives the finite-level value 1.
On an open smooth curve, the localization triangle and trace commute with finite-level reduction; no ordinary-cohomology substitute for compact support is used.
A smooth divisor class is compatible under reduction, integral realization and rationalization.

sources.match: The derived mapping-limit argument, internal-Hom reduction and rationalization support transport of specified morphisms, with finiteness supplying the extra Hom-limit conclusion.

sources.locator: §2.2, p.72 (derived coefficient Tor sequence); 2.2.16, p.73 (adic Hom/Milnor sequence)
sources.match: The comparison of adic Hom with finite-level Hom has a lim¹ kernel; agreement at each level alone is not a general uniqueness theorem.
Import Milnor, Mittag–Leffler, geometric finite generation/perfectness, scalar extension and compact-support comparisons.

nodes.title: Finite coefficient extension preserves duality and its morphisms
nodes.statement: For finite E⊂E′ over Q_ℓ, rings of integers O⊂O′, and separated finite-type X,Y over a field where ℓ is invertible, finite free scalar extension commutes canonically with f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f^!, internal Hom, K_X and D_X on the bounded constructible adic categories. It sends trace, evaluation, biduality, cup, Gysin and cycle-class maps to their O′-counterparts. Integral comparison uses O/λ^n→O′/λ^nO′; this is a cofinal subsequence of the λ′-adic tower, with ramification index accounted for. After inverting ℓ the same statements hold for E→E′. Use the existing perverse coefficient-extension theorem for perverse t-exactness, j_!* and IC. For an algebraic closure Ebar, form the filtered coefficient category from finite subextensions: every specified bounded constructible object, morphism and finite diagram descends to a finite subextension, and the preceding compatibilities pass to that category.
hypotheses: All scalar extensions here are finite free extensions of complete DVRs or finite coefficient-field extensions, followed by the specified filtered algebraic-extension category. An unrestricted category of all analytic Ebar-valued local systems is not used.
Integral torsion objects are retained; derived reduction O→O/λ is distinct from the flat O→O′ and E→E′ operations and is not perverse t-exact.
For Hom base change in the rational constructible category use its actual mapping complexes. No assertion that a simple object remains simple after coefficient extension is made.
The operation and mate identities are canonical enhanced comparisons over arbitrary k in this range; their proof does not use the separably-closed-field Hom-limit uniqueness theorem.
proofSteps: Finite free extension is exact and can be computed by a finite direct sum after choosing a basis; canonical O-linear operation comparisons are isomorphisms by that calculation. Apply the operation-reduction result to the cofinal λ^nO′ tower and its ramification comparison.

Compare the adjunction units/counits and tensor-Hom evaluations under scalar extension. Their mates yield the duality and trace identities; the finite-level constructions of EDC.3 yield the cycle/Gysin identities.

Use the imported rationalization, finite-coefficient descent of Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14 and the existing rational-perverse-coefficient-extension node. Finite diagrams and their coherence data descend together; the filtered-colimit construction is owned by the imported coefficient category.
acceptance: At a point O/λ extends to O′/λO′, whose length over O′ is the ramification index; replacing it by O′/λ′ would lose the integral information.
On P¹ the trace of the extended first Chern class is still 1∈O′ and 1∈E′.
For a smooth divisor, extension commutes with its localization boundary/Gysin map; EDC.5 supplies the separate integral perverse reduction amplitude [−1,0].

sources.match: Finite extension, rationalization and descent of constructible coefficients supply the scalar categories in which the operation comparisons are made.

Rationalization and rational Artin comparison retain the stable-lattice condition on analytic strata. Finite coefficient-subfield descent is supplied by Bhatt–Scholze 6.8.14, not by the rational Artin essential-image statement.

nodes.title: Tate coefficients and the complex orientation line
nodes.statement: For a smooth separated finite-type complex scheme X of pure complex dimension d, let or_X be the integral local orientation system of the real 2d-manifold X^an supplied by AlgebraicTopology Stage 6. For n≥1 put ζ_n=exp(2πi/ℓ^n). Construct the compatible coefficient identifications θ_{X,n}:(Z/ℓ^n(d))^an≃or_X⊗Z/ℓ^n sending ζ_n^{⊗d} to the positive complex local orientation generator. Equivalently first identify the analytic Tate line with Z(1)/ℓ^n, Z(1)=2πiZ, using the exponential sequence, and identify Z(d) with or_X. Pass these maps through the imported normalized topological realization to Z_ℓ and then O,E and finite coefficient extensions. For disconnected X use the orientation system componentwise; the integral object is a coefficient sheaf identification, not a global fundamental class on a noncompact space.
hypotheses: Smooth X, separated and finite type over C, pure complex dimension d; the complex analytic/singular realization and orientation-system carrier are imported.

The compatible positive roots ζ_n are part of the trivialization convention. The intrinsic Z(d)/orientation comparison is conjugation compatible. Arbitrary root choices cannot be silently substituted.
No de Rham comparison or field isomorphism C≃Ebar is needed for finite, integral or rational ℓ-adic Betti comparison.
proofSteps: Use the Kummer/exponential comparison to identify the analytic Tate coefficient with the reduction of 2πiZ. Tensor d times and use the complex orientation of the tangent space to identify that integral line with the local orientation system, as in BBD 6.1.4.
Check compatibility of the roots under ζ_{n+1}^ℓ=ζ_n, étale pullback and products. Apply EllAdicRealization Layer 10 to the system, not an independently defined constant topological Z_ℓ sheaf.
Extend coefficients by the finite-extension theorem and record the effect of changing the compatible root generator.
acceptance: The construction passes the unit tests listed below, and its integral reduction squares commute for every n.

sources.match: The exponential Tate line and complex orientation line agree canonically before trivialization; this pins the sign and the fundamental trace normalization.
Import the analytic coefficient site, sheaf/singular comparison and finite-level Artin maps.
Import the Z_ℓ/Q_ℓ normalized topological realization and Artin comparison. Its finite O/E coefficient extension is part of the precise request to the same owner.

uses.how: Identifies the coefficient of the local fundamental class and the target of the compact-support trace.
Pins orientation and divisor-class normalizations in comparison of local and global cohomology.
Ensures the chosen Tate trivialization survives finite coefficient extensions.

api.name: tateOrientation_finite
api.statement: Expose θ_{X,n} as an isomorphism of coefficient sheaves, with ζ_n^{⊗d} mapped to the positive local generator.

api.name: tateOrientation_ext
api.statement: Two Z/ℓ^n-linear coefficient-sheaf maps from the analytic Tate line agree if their maps on every stalk agree on ζ_n^{⊗d}. In particular the map sending this generator to the positive local orientation generator is unique.

api.name: tateOrientation_reduction
api.statement: For m≥n the reduction of θ_{X,m} is θ_{X,n}; identity and triple reduction squares commute.

api.name: tateOrientation_etalePullback
api.statement: For an étale map between smooth pure-d-dimensional complex schemes, the orientation pullback identifies the pullback of θ with θ on the source; identities and compositions agree.

api.name: tateOrientation_product
api.statement: For smooth X of dimension d and Y of dimension e, the product orientation and Tate tensor isomorphisms identify θ_{X×Y} with θ_X⊠θ_Y, with the fixed ordered product convention.

api.name: tateOrientation_coefficientExtension
api.statement: Extension Z_ℓ→O→O′ or E→E′ carries θ to the corresponding coefficient comparison; its constant integral realization uses EllAdicRealization’s comparison with the existing Mathlib Scheme.ellAdicSheaf.

api.name: tateOrientation_changeGenerator
api.statement: If the chosen compatible root generator is replaced by its u-th power, u∈Z_ℓ^×, the untwisting map that sends the new generator to the same positive orientation is u^(−d) times the original map.

api.name: tateOrientation_conjugation
api.statement: Under the canonical antiholomorphic map X^an→(conjugate X)^an, conjugation sends the positive orientation generator and the d-th Tate generator to (−1)^d times their corresponding generators. The intrinsic twisted comparison commutes with this map; no real descent or conjugation automorphism of X is assumed.

tests.name: tateOrientation_point
tests.statement: For a point (d=0), θ is the identity coefficient identification, for every root choice. Its integral constant realization agrees with the imported comparison to Mathlib Scheme.ellAdicSheaf and its cohomology with Scheme.EllAdicCohomology.

tests.name: tateOrientation_line_sign
tests.statement: On A¹(C), ζ_n maps to the orientation determined by the ordered real basis (1,i); using −i reverses this generator.

tests.name: tateOrientation_product_two_lines
tests.statement: On A²(C) the product of the two positive line generators is the positive real four-dimensional orientation; simultaneous conjugation preserves it.

tests.name: tateOrientation_changed_root
tests.statement: For d=1 and ℓ=5, replacing ζ_n by ζ_n² multiplies the fixed-orientation untwisting map by 2^−1 modulo 5^n. Keeping the original map fails to send the new generator to 1.

nodes.title: Betti comparison preserves purity, trace and supported Gysin classes
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth separated finite type over C, pure dimension d, and i:Z→X a smooth closed subscheme of pure codimension c. For Λ=Z/ℓ^n, O or E use the imported finite/integral/rational Artin comparison and the Tate-orientation identification. Analytification identifies the trace-normalized purity map i^!Λ_X≃Λ_Z(−c)[−2c] with topological purity from the complex orientation of the normal bundle. The supported fundamental class η_Z∈H_Z^{2c}(X,Λ(c)), its image cl_X(Z), and the Gysin morphism all correspond to the topological Thom/supported class, its cohomology image and the topological Gysin map. The Kummer first Chern class corresponds to the topological c₁; hence cl_X(D)=c₁(O(D)) for a smooth divisor D on both sides. The smooth absolute dualizing complex Λ(d)[2d], compact-support trace, cup/evaluation pairing and derived compact-support duality commute with comparison. For nonproper X integration uses compact support and local orientation; on proper X it specializes to the global oriented fundamental class.
hypotheses: Use bounded constructible finite-Tor input complexes for tensor/evaluation; integral O is regular. Finite-level Artin comparison is ComplexComparison Layers 10–12; adic topological realization is EllAdicRealization Layer 10.

For general singular cycles, use EDC.3/fundamental-class and cycle-class-map with their semi-purity and rational-equivalence hypotheses; this node establishes the smooth-pair normalization used by that imported extension.

Topological local orientation, relative cohomology and cup/cap are imported from AlgebraicTopology Stage 6 and its prerequisite stages. The additional supported Thom/Gysin and noncompact integral-duality interface is an exact Part II request, recorded as a gap rather than attributed to the compact-manifold scope of Stage 6.
proofSteps: Start with finite-coefficient Artin comparison and its closed/open localization and Rf_! maps. BBD 6.1.2, pp.149–151 compares f^! by local closed/smooth factorization: closed support uses localization, and the smooth factor uses purity. Apply the orientation-line identification to the absolute dualizing object. This avoids assuming a right adjoint on an unrestricted rational analytic category.

For the smooth closed immersion use local coordinates for the smooth pair and topological local orientation of C^c; complex orientation and the Kummer/exponential sequence give the same normal-coordinate generator. Glue using localization and the supported EDC.3 construction. This comparison is of specified purity maps, not just their one-dimensional cohomology groups.

Compare finite-level trace with local orientation integration using BBD 6.1.4. Cup/evaluation and Rf_! compatibility give derived compact-support duality. Pass the coherent finite-level comparisons through the requested normalized topological O-realization, using strict reduction and completeness; the geometric mapping-limit result verifies the specified integral maps. Rationalize and extend finite coefficients. At E-level retain the stable-lattice Artin essential image; do not invoke an equivalence with all analytic E-local systems.

For a divisor compare its supported class and first Chern class using EDC.3 and the Kummer/exponential diagram. The equality follows with the positive convention; arbitrary units are accounted for by the orientation API.
acceptance: P¹(C): c₁(O(1)) is the positive class and its trace is +1 at finite, integral and rational levels.
U=P¹ minus r≥1 distinct points: H_c²(U,Λ(1))≃Λ with trace 1 on the positive generator; the boundary segment Λ→Λ^r→H_c¹(U,Λ) has the diagonal first map. In contrast H²(U,Λ)=0.

For a smooth divisor D in a smooth proper complex X, the supported algebraic class maps to the positive Thom class, and both routes to H²(X^an,Λ) give c₁(O(D)); the square commutes before forgetting support.
For disconnected X, trace sums the component traces; no connectedness-free assertion H_c^{2d}(X,Λ(d))≃Λ is made.

sources.match: The operation-compatible constructible comparison and exponential orientation normalization supply compatibility of the specified duality and supported-class morphisms.
Import sheaf/singular, compact-support, cup and relative Artin comparison rather than a second construction.
Import the normalized Z_ℓ/Q_ℓ topological realization, and request its finite O/E extension, through which the coherent finite-level identities pass.

nodes.title: Smooth trace comparison on algebraically realized analytic spaces
nodes.statement: Let k be a complete nontrivially rank-one valued nonarchimedean field, f:X→Y a separated finite-type smooth morphism of pure relative dimension d between finite-type k-schemes, and f^an:X^an→Y^an its actual analytification over Spa(k,k°). Assume the analytic map is taut and its target quasi-separated, and n is prime to the residue characteristic. Under the imported comparison (Rf_!K)^an≃Rf^an_!(K^an), the analytified scheme trace Rf_!f^*L(d)[2d]→L equals Huber’s analytic smooth trace, and the trace-normalized purity/adjunction maps f^!L≃f^*L(d)[2d] compare with (f^an)^!L^an≃(f^an)^*L^an(d)[2d]. For a smooth pair i:Z→X, the corresponding supported smooth-pair fundamental class and Gysin map agree with their analytified maps. This transports the given algebraic model; it neither assigns models to arbitrary analytic spaces nor enlarges analytic duality to residue-characteristic torsion.
hypotheses: Λ=Z/n, n≥1 prime to residue characteristic, and L bounded below; for bounded constructible duality restrict to actual finite-Tor inputs and bounds. H3/general-analytic-smooth-trace already supplies the shifted-constant trace, in a broader coefficient range. The requested H3 smooth-duality extension supplies the full D⁺ trace-normalized adjunction used here, in Huber’s narrower range.

Use scheme-fibre-product analytification from AdicSpacesPartII and finite-dimensional, separated/taut analytic support hypotheses. General finite-type field direct-image comparison Huber 3.8.1 needs n prime to char(k) in positive characteristic; this weaker condition in characteristic zero does not extend the smooth-duality range.
Integral analytic realization is not inferred from finite-coefficient comparison without a normalized analytic coefficient category and uniform bounds; its exact extension is recorded separately.
proofSteps: Import Huber 5.7.2’s proper-support comparison (and its pseudo-adic version 5.7.5) through the existing analytic owner. For proper maps use H5/proper-comparison-3-7-2 and for open embeddings use extension by zero; glue through the compactification comparison.

Import H3/general-analytic-smooth-trace and its chart, composition, pullback and P¹ normalization, rather than plan another trace. Huber 7.3.4 constructs the all-dimensional trace on local étale affine charts from the algebraic trace by 5.7.5; compare the chartwise normalized constructions and glue on the given algebraic model.
Huber 7.5.3–7.5.4 identify that trace with the exceptional adjunction counit. Taking the trace-normalized adjoint gives the stated smooth-purity comparison.

For a smooth closed pair apply transitivity of exceptional pullback to the two smooth structure maps, then their trace-normalized purity formulas, to obtain codimension-c purity. The proper closed/open localization comparisons transport the supported EDC.3 class and its Gysin map. This is smooth-pair purity on an algebraic model; arbitrary regular analytic pairs are outside the claim. Import H3/analytic-first-chern-class for the Kummer normalization already compared with schemes.
acceptance: P¹_k: the algebraic and analytic finite-level trace send c₁(O(1)) to 1; this is tested on the actual analytification.
A¹_k and G_m,k: comparison respects the compact-support localization sequence and its curve trace.
A smooth algebraic divisor has the same supported class and Gysin normalization after analytification; a rigid closed disc is not declared the analytification of A¹_k.

sources.locator: Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1, pp.226–228; Theorems 5.7.2 and 5.7.5, pp.316–318
sources.match: These supply proper/direct/proper-support comparison on actual algebraic analytifications, with distinct coefficient hypotheses.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.3.4 and proof, pp.378–382; Theorem 7.5.3 and Lemma 7.5.4(ii) and proof, pp.390–392
sources.match: The trace is defined locally from the scheme trace in every dimension and identifies smooth purity with the adjunction counit. The residue-characteristic restriction is part of this result.

nodes.title: Scheme/diamond trace mates and the essential-image condition
nodes.statement: Let f:Y→X be separated finite type between qcqs characteristic-p schemes (or the perfection of such a morphism), and take the eligible discrete prime-to-p or regular adic coefficients of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons. Put F=Rf_!, F◇=Rf◇_!, and let c_X^*⊣Rc_X*, c_Y^*⊣Rc_Y*. The imported comparison α:c_X^*F≃F◇c_Y^* has right-adjoint mate β:f^!Rc_X*≃Rc_Y*(f◇)^!. These are compatible with the exceptional adjunction counits: for B on X◇, the map F f^!Rc_X*B→Rc_X*B recovered from the diamond counit F◇(f◇)^!B→B, using α’s right-adjoint mate and β, is the scheme counit. For a:Y→Spec k and B=c_k^*Λ this recovers K_Y and D_Y through Rc_Y* and recovers the trace/evaluation morphisms. Strong c_Y^*f^!A≃(f◇)^!c_X^*A follows precisely when that diamond exceptional object belongs to the essential image of c_Y^*; its comparison is the counit after β and the scheme unit. The same test applies to the internal-Hom object defining diamond duality. This node proves the mate compatibility and the conditional criterion, not the missing geometric essential-image assertion.
hypotheses: The diamond map is compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds and of finite dim.trg, as supplied by ECD 27.4. The dualizing complex is relative to B=(Spec k)◇, with its actual structure map.

For mixed-characteristic finite-type schemes over a complete DVR with perfect residue field, use L4/27.5 for α and β, and L6/27.7 only for the scheme unit on bounded constructible finite prime-to-residue-characteristic objects A and the recovered candidate T=f^!A, with explicit constructibility and finite-Tor witnesses. Use the ambient adjunction and the recovered constructible candidate; do not assert global ambient full faithfulness or a right adjoint between restricted bounded constructible categories. Characteristic-p and DVR constructions of (Spec k)◇ have different plus-ring/base conventions.

Internal Hom and tensor are ambient derived operations; bounded constructible restrictions require their own witnesses. Neither full faithfulness of c^* nor right-adjoint recovery implies that every diamond object is in its essential image.
proofSteps: Use L3’s exact α, β and internal-Hom right-adjoint identity. Define δ_C:F Rc_Y*C→Rc_X*F◇C by adjunction from c_X*F Rc_Y*C→F◇c_Y*Rc_Y*C→F◇C using α and the c_Y counit. The mate/triangle identities give ε_scheme at Rc_X*B = (Rc_X*ε◇_B) ∘ δ_(f◇!B) ∘ F(β_B), with source F f^!Rc_X*B and target Rc_X*B. This proves compatibility of the actual counits.

Use the full-faithfulness unit to recover a^!Λ and then apply Rc_Y* RHom(c_Y^*K,B)=RHom(K,Rc_Y*B) to recover scheme duality. This is the verified content of the existing diamond-transport-of-duality node.

For a desired strong object comparison compose c_Y^* of β with the counit at the relevant diamond object. The pinned Mathlib counit/essential-image criterion makes the exact additional hypothesis explicit. Record the unresolved geometric preservation input as a gap, rather than deducing it from full faithfulness.

Apply the same mate calculation to L4’s α and β in their own base convention. Import L6’s unit theorem only on the particular eligible finite constructible objects. Put T=f^!A and B=(f◇)^!c_X^*A; the scheme unit at A and β give e:Rc_Y*B≃T. If the unit at T is invertible, the canonical c_Y^*T→B is invertible exactly when B is isomorphic to c_Y^*T. This pointwise candidate criterion uses ambient adjunction triangle identities, not ambient full faithfulness or an adjunction between bounded restrictions. No exceptional-image preservation follows from 27.7.
acceptance: For f the identity, both mates and recovered counit are identities.
For f étale, f^!=f^* and the known pullback comparison supplies the strong exceptional comparison in this restricted case.
For P¹ in characteristic p, recover the scheme trace of c₁(O(1)) as 1 through Rc_*; do not replace this test by an unproved absolute diamond dualizing-object identity.

The inclusion of the zero-object category into vector spaces is fully faithful and has a right adjoint sending every vector space to the zero object. Its counit 0→V is not invertible for nonzero V. This concrete categorical check prevents inferring an image theorem from right-adjoint recovery.

In the DVR range, for T=f^!A with invertible unit and recovered B, test the criterion B≃c_Y^*T directly. Membership in the image of an unspecified nonconstructible scheme object is not substituted for this particular candidate.
